title: Authentication Service sessions: admin inactivity timeout, the service-enrollment session and forced Private Access reauthentication
aliases: Force Authentication for Private Access Reauthentication

prose.text: Authentication Service tracks who is signed in with sessions, set on its Authentication Session page. {{session-based}}

prose.label: IdP options.
prose.text: {{hosted-option-default}} Which setting those options belong to is open {{gap:idp-options-setting}}.

prose.label: Token lifetime.
prose.text: Where an API client token lifetime is set is open {{gap:token-lifetime}}.

prose.label: Permission.
prose.text: Changing these is the Authentication Session module: [[zidentity.admin-rbac.permissions:authentication-session]].

checks.do: Whether a user is asked to reauthenticate because the session timeout expired or because Force Authentication for Private Access Reauthentication is enabled, and whether Authentication Session for Service Entitlement is enabled.
Whether User Single Sign-On is enabled for the tenant, since the force reauthentication option is shown only then.

session-based.statement: Authentication Service uses session-based authentication to keep track of authenticated users or enrolled services.

quotes: Authentication Service uses session-based authentication to keep track of the authenticated users or enrolled services.

admin-inactivity-timeout.statement: Administrator Inactivity Timeout Duration is the period, in minutes, after which the user is logged out of the Authentication Service session, settable from 5 to 600 minutes (10 hours).

quotes: Administrator Inactivity Timeout Duration (in Minutes): Enter the timeout period after which the user is logged out of the Authentication Service session. You can set the timeout period from 5 to 600 minutes (10 hours).

service-entitlement-session.statement: Authentication Session for Service Entitlement applies the Authentication Service session to Zscaler services during user enrollment. It is disabled by default, since Authentication Service sends users to the organization's IdP; enabled, Authentication Service can verify active sessions locally based on the Service Enrollment Session Timeout instead of always redirecting users to the IdP.

quotes: Authentication Session for Service Entitlement: Enable to apply the authenticated session of Authentication Service to Zscaler services during user enrollment.
This option is disabled by default, as Authentication Service sends users to the organization's identity provider (IdP) for authentication.
If enabled, Authentication Service can locally verify active sessions based on the Service Enrollment Session Timeout value, instead of always redirecting users to the IdP.

local-session-examples.statement: The page gives these examples beside the Authentication Session for Service Entitlement option: for Private Access reauthentication through Client Connector, and for browser-based access through Internet & SaaS or Private Access, a still-valid session is authenticated locally by Authentication Service and an expired one is redirected to the external IdP.

quotes: Private Access (ZPA) reauthentication through Zscaler Client Connector: During reauthentication, if the existing session is still valid, Authentication Service authenticates the user locally. If the session is expired, the user is redirected to the external IdP.

Browser-based access through Internet & SaaS (ZIA) or Private Access: During user's access to Zscaler service through a browser, if the existing session is still valid, Authentication Service authenticates the user locally. If the session is expired, the user is redirected to the external IdP.

service-enrollment-timeout.statement: Service Enrollment Session Timeout is the period, in minutes, after which the user's service session expires and the user must reauthenticate, settable from 5 to 600 minutes (10 hours).

quotes: Service Enrollment Session Timeout (in Minutes): Enter the timeout period after which the user's service session expires, and the user is required to reauthenticate. You can set the timeout period from 5 to 600 minutes (10 hours).

force-zpa-reauth.statement: Force Authentication for Private Access Reauthentication decides whether users are prompted when Private Access requests reauthentication: disabled, the IdP decides; enabled, Authentication Service tells the IdP to ignore existing sessions and force reauthentication each time, by sending forceauth=true (SAML) or prompt=login (OIDC). The option is shown only when User Single Sign-On is enabled for the tenant.

quotes: Force Authentication for Private Access Reauthentication: This option determines whether to prompt the users to reauthenticate when Private Access requests reauthentication.
When this option is disabled, the IdP decides if reauthentication is required for a user.

When enabled, Authentication Service instructs the IdP to ignore existing user sessions and force reauthentication each time Private Access requests it by sending a parameter (for SAML protocol: forceauth=true and for OIDC protocol: prompt=login).
This option is shown only when User Single Sign-On (SSO) is enabled for your tenant.

hosted-option-default.statement: By default only the Hosted option is shown for all tenants; options for third-party IdPs are also listed, depending on the external IdPs configured for the tenant.

quotes: By default, only the Hosted option is shown for all tenants. The options for third-party IdPs are also listed, depending on the external IdPs configured for the tenant.

timeout-defaults.title: The default of the admin inactivity and service enrollment timeouts
timeout-defaults.detail: The page gives the 5 to 600 minute range of each timeout and does not state a default for either.
timeout-defaults.blocks: stating how long an idle admin or enrolled service stays signed in on an unconfigured tenant

idp-options-setting.title: Which Authentication Session setting the Hosted and third-party IdP options belong to
idp-options-setting.detail: The page says that by default only the Hosted option is shown, with options for third-party IdPs listed by the tenant's external IdPs; it does not say which setting they belong to.
idp-options-setting.blocks: reading the Authentication Session page for a tenant with external IdPs

token-lifetime.title: Where an API client access token lifetime is set
token-lifetime.detail: The Authentication Session page lists the admin inactivity timeout, the service-entitlement session, the service enrollment timeout and forced Private Access reauthentication, and no token-lifetime setting. That is an absence in one page, so where the lifetime is configured is not answered here (see zidentity.api-clients:tenant-default-lifetime).
token-lifetime.blocks: answering how long an API client token lives
